title: Prevention of venous thromboembolism in cirrhotic patients with hepatocellular carcinoma
official: Prevention of venous thromboembolism in cirrhotic patients with hepatocellular carcinoma
summary: Main objective: To explore the efficacy of prophylactic LMWH therapy in preventing thrombotic events in consecutive adult participants with cirrhosis of any etiology, CSPH, and HCC with a TTV of > or = 5 cm³, who are candidates for locoregional treatments, without evidence of thrombosis at the time of enrollment
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Written informed consent
2. ability and willingness to comply with the protocol
3. adults (≥ 18 years)
4. male or female participants
5. liver cirrhosis of any etiology
6. CSPH
7. HCC with TTV > or = 5 cm³, candidates for locoregional treatments
Exclusion criteria:
1. hypersensitivity to tinzaparin or to any of the excipients
2. history of major bleeding defined as bleeding occurring in a critical site (intracranial, intraspinal, intraocular, retroperitoneal, intra-articular, pericardial, intrauterine, or intramuscular with compartment syndrome)
3. recent portal hypertension-related bleeding (< 3 months)
4. current septic endocarditis
5. evidence of venous thromboembolism event at baseline
6. history of prior venous thromboembolic events
7. current anticoagulant therapy
8. severe liver dysfunction (Child-Pugh class C)
9. participation in another clinical trial in which an investigational drug was administered within 30 days prior to screening or within 5 half-lives of the study drug, whichever is longer
10. hepatic encephalopathy of a severity that precludes the ability to provide informed consent (West Haven grade ≥2)
11. poor prognosis (estimated survival time of less than 12 months)
12. international normalized ratio (INR) > 2
13. congenital coagulation or platelet disorder
14. active malignancy other than HCC
15. severe renal failure (GFR <30 mL/min)
16. platelet count <30,000/mm³
17. pregnancy or breastfeeding
18. current or previous immune-mediated heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT type II)
